record.original_question: In full-information online learning, does there exist an algorithm such that for every ε > 0 it simultaneously achieves regret at most O(√(Σ_t Var_{π∼Pt}(ℓt(π(xt))) · log(1/ε))) against the top ε-quantile of policies, where Pt is the algorithm's distribution over policies at round t?

evidence.quote: An unresolved COLT 2016 open problem of Freund (2016) asks whether there exists an algorithm for this setting with regret at most O( √ ∑ T t=1 Varπ∼Pt (ℓt(π(xt))) ⋅ log(1/ε)) against the top ε-quantile of policies for all ε > 0 simultaneously.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following full-information online learning setting. Let $\Pi$ be a (possibly infinite) set of policies, where each policy $\pi \in \Pi$ maps contexts $x \in \mathcal{X}$ to actions in some set $\mathcal{A}$. Play proceeds in rounds $t = 1, 2, \dots, T$. At each round $t$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The learner chooses a probability distribution $P_t$ over $\Pi$.
\item A context $x_t \in \mathcal{X}$ and a loss function $\ell_t : \mathcal{A} \to [0,1]$ are revealed (chosen by an oblivious or adaptive adversary).
\item The learner samples $\pi_t \sim P_t$, plays $\pi_t(x_t)$, and incurs loss $\ell_t(\pi_t(x_t))$. The full loss function $\ell_t$ is observed.
\end{enumerate}

For a distribution $Q$ over $\Pi$, define the $\varepsilon$-quantile regret as
\[
R_T(Q,\varepsilon) \;=\; \sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathbb{E}_{\pi \sim P_t}[\ell_t(\pi(x_t))] \;-\; \inf_{S \subseteq \Pi : Q(S) \ge \varepsilon} \; \sup_{\pi \in S} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \ell_t(\pi(x_t)),
\]
i.e., the cumulative loss of the algorithm minus the cumulative loss of the best policy among the top $\varepsilon$-fraction (under a fixed prior $Q$) of policies. Let
\[
V_T \;=\; \sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathrm{Var}_{\pi \sim P_t}\bigl(\ell_t(\pi(x_t))\bigr).
\]

\textbf{Question.} Does there exist an algorithm (specifying the sequence of distributions $P_t$) such that, simultaneously for every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$,
\[
R_T(Q,\varepsilon) \;=\; O\!\left(\sqrt{V_T \cdot \log(1/\varepsilon)}\right) ?
\]
artifact.status_search_result: The question, posed as a COLT 2016 open problem, asks for a single algorithm achieving a second-order (variance-based) regret bound that simultaneously holds against the top ε-quantile of policies for every ε > 0. Searches turned up the original COLT 2016 open-problem write-up and related work (e.g., Squint / Koolen–Van Erven on second-order quantile methods), as well as later sources that still describe the problem as unresolved in this exact form. No publication claiming a full resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Second order regret bounds based on scaling time (Freund, COLT 2016)
status_evidence.snippet: Freund proposes a second-order regret bound and conjectures it is satisfied by NormalHedge.
status_evidence.claim: Original posing of the open problem at COLT 2016.

status_evidence.title: Second-order Quantile Methods for Experts and Combinatorial Games (Koolen, Van Erven)
status_evidence.snippet: First bounds that are simultaneously second-order and quantile-based (Squint algorithm), but not in the form Freund asks for.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial progress on second-order quantile regret, predating and not resolving Freund's specific conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Model Selection for Contextual Bandits
status_evidence.snippet: References Freund (2016) as an unresolved COLT open problem.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2020 the problem was still listed as unresolved.
